notes: §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR2: "If implementor-name-1 does not reference an external switch, the associated mnemonic-name may be specified only in the ACCEPT, DISPLAY, SEND, or WRITE statements. A condition-name cannot be associated with such an implementor-name." No edition arm is involved; the 2023 split into device-names and feature-names is the implementor's own table, which 1985 leaves to the implementor too. Second sentence: Unavailable refuses an ON STATUS or OFF STATUS phrase on a name whose row is not a switch, and BindImplementorNameEntry reports it as COBOL2241 and registers nothing (probed at 85 on CONSOLE and C01, with and without a mnemonic-name). First sentence: a mnemonic-name is known only to the MnemonicRegistry, which four statements read, MnemonicDevice (ACCEPT FROM, DISPLAY UPON: a device's), MnemonicOperand and FeatureAdvancing (WRITE ADVANCING: a feature's), ScreenSendAdvancing (SEND ADVANCING: a feature's) and SwitchBindSet, which refuses a non-switch mnemonic with COBOL1757; anywhere else the word resolves as no data-name or procedure-name and is refused with COBOL1639 (probed at 85: IF, MOVE, ADD, STRING, INSPECT, CALL USING, PERFORM). Probed at 85: DISPLAY UPON and ACCEPT FROM a device mnemonic, WRITE and SEND ADVANCING a feature mnemonic compile. The witness is CONSOLE IS CONS ON STATUS IS CONS-ON, refused with COBOL2241.

next.reason: 1985: a non-switch implementor-name's mnemonic-name 'may be specified only in the ACCEPT, DISPLAY, SEND, or WRITE statements', with no condition-name. 2023 splits the names: §2023:12.3.7.3 SR6 'Mnemonic-name-2 may be specified only in the WRITE statement' (feature-names) and §2023:12.3.7.3 SR7 'Mnemonic-name-3 may be specified only in the ACCEPT and DISPLAY statements' (device-names), each letting the implementor add restrictions; SEND is no longer listed. §2023:12.3.7.2 still allows ON/OFF STATUS condition-names only on switch-name-1. The set of statements allowed for a given mnemonic differs.
